predecessors.name: Ottoman Empire
predecessors.text: the Ottoman Sanjak of Montenegro: "In 1514, Zeta was separated from the Sanjak of Scutari and established as the separate Sanjak of Montenegro" under Skenderbeg Crnojević (to 1528)

successors.name: Montenegro (Principality, Kingdom and Republic)
successors.text: the secular Principality of Montenegro: Danilo "turned his land into a secular principality" in 1852

ledger.x: 1516: the clans elect Vavila prince-bishop, founding the Prince-Bishopric (the page: "prince-bishops of Cetinje ruled from 1516 until 1852").

1767: the Prince-Bishopric is "temporarily abolished in 1767-1773" when the impostor Šćepan Mali "posed as the Russian Emperor" and the Montenegrins accepted him as emperor (1766-1768); the metropolitans return in 1773.
1785: Kara Mahmud attacks Montenegro, "crossing Bjelice before withdrawing" (Petar I page); the Scutari pashalik's own page says he "conquered it in just four days".
1789: "The Ottoman Porte formally recognized Montenegro's independence under Petar I" (main page; the Petar I page dates a Russian subsidy to 1799).
22 September 1796: Petar I defeats Kara Mahmud at Krusi (after Martinići): "The Montenegrin victory resulted in territorial expansion".
22 September 1796: Kara Mahmud is killed at Krusi and his army defeated; Montenegro keeps its mountains.
1806: war over the Bay of Kotor, which the Treaty of Pressburg (1805) had set to pass from Habsburg to French rule (Bay page).
1807: "The Treaty of Tilsit gave control of the Bay of Kotor to France"; Petar I's plan to unite the Bay, Herzegovina, Dubrovnik and Dalmatia is thwarted.
1813: Montenegrins with Russian and British support free the Bay of Kotor from the French and declare its union with Montenegro.
1815: "the bay was annexed by the Austrian Empire" and joined to the province of Dalmatia.
13 March 1852: Danilo renounces his ecclesiastical character, takes the title of knjaz and turns the Prince-Bishopric into the secular Principality of Montenegro.

wars.name: War of Cyprus
wars.outcome: Montenegrins fought for Venice under Pahomije; no change of Montenegro's land recorded.

wars.name: War of Candia
wars.outcome: Montenegrins fought on Venice's side; no change of land recorded.

wars.name: Morean War
wars.outcome: Montenegrins fought, including at the 1687 Battle of Herceg Novi; no change of Montenegro's own land recorded.

wars.name: Kara Mahmud Bushati's campaigns against Montenegro
wars.outcome: Defeat in June 1785; victories at Martinići (July) and Krusi (22 September 1796) in which Kara Mahmud was killed; the Bjelopavlići and Piperi joined Montenegro.

wars.name: Montenegrin-Russian war with France over the Bay of Kotor
wars.outcome: The Bay passed to France at Tilsit (1807), was freed and united with Montenegro in 1813, and was annexed by Austria in 1815.

certainty.note: Tribal territories with no surveyed frontier; the 1813 Bay of Kotor union and the 1796 Hills are approximate.
